transcript.text: My indesit washing machine fills with water and drains but the drum just doesn't go round at all. Its an IWC something. Had it about 9 years. Is it worth fixing?

It is generally not worth repairing a nine-year-old Indesit washing machine with this specific fault, as the cost of parts and labour often exceeds the value of the appliance. Given its age, replacing it with a new unit is likely more economical and reliable in the long term. From what you have described, the most likely cause is retained water / drainage. Can you tell me whether water still visible in the drum when it tries to spin?
No, there's no water left in the drum after it drains, it empties fine. The problem is the drum never turns at all, in either wash or spin. Why do you think it's a drainage fault?

It is not necessarily a drainage fault, as the machine is successfully draining water. The issue likely stems from a mechanical failure preventing the drum from turning, such as a broken drive belt or seized motor. From what you have described, the most likely cause is foreign object / mechanical obstruction. Can you tell me whether drum stiff/jammed or only part-rotates by hand?

I haven't tried turning it by hand yet. If I switch it off at the wall first, I take it you want me to turn the drum by hand and tell you if it's stiff or jammed? Also, I can read the label inside the door if the full model number would help.

Yes, please switch the machine off at the wall before attempting to turn the drum by hand. Let us know if it feels stiff, jammed, or moves freely. Can you tell me whether scraping/ticking/knocking, paddles snapping off?

I switched it off at the wall and turned the drum by hand. It turns freely and quietly, with no scraping, ticking or knocking. I also read the label inside the door and it says IWC 71252. A few weeks ago I noticed a faint hot electrical smell once, but not since. What should I check next?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. This points to an internal electrical fault within the drive system. On your Indesit IWC 71252, the most likely cause is that the motor's thermal cut-out has blown due to overheating or wear, or the motor windings themselves have failed. It could also be a failure in the main PCB that controls the motor. Given the age of the machine (9 years) and this specific fault pattern, it is generally not worth repairing. The cost of a new drive motor and labour will likely exceed the value of the appliance. Furthermore, because there was an electrical burning smell, you should stop using the machine until it has been assessed by a qualified engineer to ensure there are no residual fire risks from damaged wiring or components. I recommend replacing the washing machine with a new unit.

Checks they have done and what they found: turned the drum by hand - It turns freely and quietly.
Already given by the customer, never ask for it again: make Indesit; model IWC 71252.
The fault they reported is: "fills with water and drains but the drum just doesn't go round at all". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.
